negative_findings.description: No banking-sector reference material was surfaced for Slovanet a.s. in this pass; Slovanet appeared only as a client in another integrator's telecom reference list, not as a supplier to banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovanet reads as a telco/connectivity provider rather than a bank software supplier; it may still supply WAN/connectivity to banks but no public evidence found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keeping an unqualified actor in the competitor set would distort the SK supplier map; it should be demoted to a connectivity-layer supplier pending evidence.

negative_findings.description: Trask (CZ consultancy) could not be linked to Slovak banking delivery in this pass; queries returned Erste Group/Erste Digital material instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: No SK-specific Trask reference, office or project page found; the 'Trask/Erste' pairing in the cell definition is unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If Trask is not materially present in SK, the CZ-consultancy channel into SK banks runs through other firms and needs separate discovery.

negative_findings.description: Neither Gratex International nor DATALAN yielded a current, first-party banking reference page in search results; only third-party profiles (FinReg, RocketReach, a stale directory mirror) and an insurance-portal case study surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Their live corporate domains and reference sections remain unverified; possible site restructuring or corporate reorganisation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of the larger named SK integrators are currently under-evidenced, leaving a hole in the prime-contractor map.

negative_findings.description: Ditec publishes a rich product catalogue but no client reference list naming banks; bank deployments of its e-signature stack must be inferred from other parties' materials.
negative_findings.result_summary: Product-level evidence is strong, customer-level evidence absent on the vendor's own site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Compliance-component suppliers are structurally invisible in the reference-list channel, so market share there needs a different method (tenders, conference talks, bank documentation).

coverage_gaps.description: No SK IT trade-press outlet was captured in this pass (e.g. itnews.sk, touchIT, PC REVUE, TREND) even though they carry the majority of SK integrator project announcements and interviews.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sk-language pass on 'itnews.sk banka projekt', 'touchit bankovníctvo', 'TREND IT dodávateľ banka' and add the qualifying outlets as pointer/indirect sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Primary Slovak procurement and contract registers (ÚVO/uvo.gov.sk, CRZ crz.gov.sk) were not directly captured; only the derived uvostat analytics were.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ÚVO tender notices and the Central Register of Contracts as first-party sources — they name suppliers, values and subcontractors for state-linked financial entities.

coverage_gaps.description: Job-board evidence (profesia.sk, bank and integrator career pages) was not collected, though it is the fastest indicator of which technologies SK banks and their hubs are staffing for and which integrators are ramping bank delivery teams.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add profesia.sk saved searches by technology + employer, plus career pages of Erste Digital, VÚB/Intesa, Tatra banka/RBI hubs.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-owned service hubs other than Erste Digital (e.g. hubs of VÚB/Intesa, Tatra banka/Raiffeisen, ČSOB/KBC in SK) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted pass per bank group on 'shared service centre', 'kompetenčné centrum', 'IT hub Bratislava/Košice' in sk and en.

coverage_gaps.description: Industry event programmes (ITAPA and banking/fintech conferences) were not captured; speaker lists and agendas reveal integrator-bank pairings and named projects before any case study is published.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ITAPA and SK fintech/banking conference agendas as pointer sources and mine past programmes for supplier-bank pairs.

brief: The Slovak bank IT supply chain is documented mainly through vendor-published Slovak-language 'referencie' pages, which are open, low-friction and frequently name bank clients outright — Asseco Central Europe, TEMPEST, ANASOFT/FINUS, SOFTEC, Millennium (Soitron Group), LYNX, EEA and Centire all expose usable lists, with EEA offering a segment-filtered URL. These marketing claims should be triangulated against statutory and derived data: registeruz.sk annual reports, FinStat/FinReg company financials, and uvostat's consortium analytics over public procurement, which expose prime/subcontractor relationships that no reference page admits. Two structural blind spots remain: compliance-component suppliers such as Ditec publish products but never clients, and bank-owned hubs like Erste Digital (2,000+ IT staff in Bratislava and Košice) insource work invisibly behind a LinkedIn login wall, so hiring data and conference programmes are needed as proxies. Gratex, DATALAN, Slovanet and Trask are currently under-evidenced in the banking context and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than dropped.
